glosses: An exemption from certain laws granted by the Pope.
A particular benefit, advantage, or favor; a right or immunity enjoyed by some but not others; a prerogative, preferential treatment.

examples.text: All first-year professors here must teach four courses a term, yet you're only teaching one! What entitled you to such a privilege?

glosses: An especially rare or fortunate opportunity; the good fortune (to do something).

examples.text: I had the privilege to sit near him in the House for a small part of his Commons service and there was an additional device provided to aid his participation in debates.

glosses: The fact of being privileged; the status or existence of (now especially social or economic) benefit or advantage within a given society.

examples.text: People who at any other time would cling like glue to their miserable scraps of privilege, will surrender them fast enough when their country is in danger.

examples.text: Dr Grigori Loutchansky is – according to a congressman speaking under congressional privilege – a "purported Russian mob figure".

glosses: A common law doctrine that protects certain communications from being used as evidence in court.

examples.text: Your honor, my client is not required to answer that; her response is protected by attorney-client privilege.

glosses: An ability to perform an action on the system that can be selectively granted or denied to users.

To bring or put into a condition of privilege or exemption from evil or danger; to exempt; to deliver.

glosses: Donner la priorité à quelque chose ou quelqu’un, lui accorder l’importance la plus élevée.
